explanation: Breadth-first search the implicit graph of dictionary words differing at one position. Generate each lowercase substitution and remove a word from the unvisited set when enqueuing it, so the first reached target has minimum distance. The dictionary input is not modified.
timeComplexity: O(D + 26·V·L²) expected time, where D is total dictionary character storage, V visited words and L source length. Copying the by-value dictionary includes its strings; each visited word generates 26L candidates whose creation/hashing costs O(L).
spaceComplexity: O(D + V·L) auxiliary character storage for the by-value dictionary copy and BFS candidate strings.

correctness: Every generated neighbor differs from the current word by exactly one permitted lowercase substitution and belongs to the unvisited dictionary. Breadth-first search processes words in nondecreasing path length. Marking a word visited when enqueued prevents redundant paths without losing a shorter route. Therefore the first target reached has minimum substitution count; exhausting the queue proves no permitted transformation exists.
walkthrough: Use dictionary {bike, bile, tile, tide}, source bake and target tide. The BFS reaches bike at distance 1, bile at 2, tile at 3, and tide at 4. Each step changes exactly one character: bake → bike → bile → tile → tide. No earlier layer reaches tide, so return 4.
edgeCases: Identical source and target return 0 even before searching the dictionary.
The source need not be a dictionary member; generated intermediate and target words must belong to the dictionary.
